Neonatal finless porpoises measure approximately 72.5 centimeters [Lb = approximately 72.5 centimeters] at birth, a length that reflects the constraints of in utero development within a relatively small-bodied cetacean. Newborn individuals typically weigh around 7000 grams [Wwb = around 7000 grams], a modest mass that supports a relatively brief gestation period. Under the core body temperature typical of this species (37 °C [T = 37 °C]), the gestation time from gametic union through foetal development to parturition lasts approximately 320 days [tg = approximately 320 days]. This gestation length is comparable to that of other phocoenids of similar adult body size. The neonate emerges as a precocial calf capable of swimming and nursing almost immediately, a critical adaptation for survival in dynamic coastal waters. Observations from captive breeding programs indicate that the time since birth at weaning, when the dependent newborn transitions to nutritional independence, is about 320 days [tx = about 320 days] at a temperature of 37 °C [T = 37 °C]. During this suckling juvenile phase, the calf relies entirely on maternal milk before gradually incorporating solid prey into its diet. The total length at weaning has been recorded at 101 centimeters .

As the nursing offspring progresses toward independence, the wet weight at weaning reaches approximately 24,500 grams [Wwx = approximately 24,500 grams], a value that signifies considerable mass accumulation during the lactation period. Following the cessation of suckling, the juvenile enters a prolonged sub-adult phase characterized by continued growth and behavioral development. The total length at puberty, marking the onset of gonadal maturation and reproductive activation, is attained at approximately 148 centimeters [Lp = approximately 148 centimeters]. Puberty in this species occurs after an extended period of somatic development; under standard thermal conditions of 37 °C [T = 37 °C], the time since birth at puberty has been estimated at 2190 days [tp = 2190 days]. This intraspecific plasticity in maturation timing is not unusual among small cetaceans inhabiting variable environments.

The ultimate total length of a fully grown adult finless porpoise, representing the asymptotic body size reached after the completion of the somatic growth phase, is 227 centimeters [Li = 227 centimeters]. Correspondingly, the ultimate wet weight of a reproductively active adult is approximately 72,000 grams [Wwi = approximately 72,000 grams], a mass that supports the energetic demands of a breeding adult mammal, including the costs of gestation and lactation. At the species' normal core temperature of 37 °C [T = 37 °C], the maximum recorded lifespan in the wild has been documented at 33 years [am = 33 years], a figure derived from long-term photo-identification studies. This longevity is typical for a phocoenid of this body size and suggests a relatively slow life-history pace, with extended interbirth intervals and substantial parental investment in each offspring. Senescence in this species appears to be gradual, with age-related declines in reproductive output becoming apparent only after the third decade of life.

Reproductive output in the finless porpoise is relatively modest, consistent with a K-selected life-history strategy. Females typically give birth to a single calf per reproductive event [N_R_i = single calf per reproductive event], and under optimal conditions they may produce one calf approximately every two years [Ri = one calf approximately every two years]. This low fecundity is balanced by high neonatal survival rates in undisturbed habitats. The maximum reproductive rate observed in captive individuals maintained at 37 °C [T = 37 °C] indicates that a female could theoretically produce up to 0.5 calves per year [Ri = up to 0.5 calves per year], though such rates are rarely sustained in wild populations due to energetic constraints and environmental variability. Each birth event represents a significant energetic investment for the gravid female, who must accumulate substantial lipid reserves to support both the foetal development and the subsequent lactation period.

Comparisons with other members of the family Phocoenidae reveal that the finless porpoise exhibits a life-history profile intermediate between the more rapidly maturing harbor porpoise and the slower-paced vaquita. The total length at birth of 72.5 centimeters [Lb = 72.5 centimeters] is proportionally large relative to adult size, a common trait among cetaceans that maximizes neonatal survivorship. The adult asymptotic length of 227 centimeters [Li = 227 centimeters] places Neophocaena phocaenoides among the smaller phocoenids, with correspondingly modest absolute energetic requirements. Field records indicate that the species occupies a broad thermal niche across its Indo-Pacific range, though all the life-history parameters reported here were recorded at the species' typical core body temperature of 37 °C [T = 37 °C]. The weaning length of 101 centimeters  marks a critical nutritional emancipation point, after which the juvenile must independently locate and capture prey in often turbid coastal waters. Understanding these measurement-based benchmarks is essential for constructing accurate population models and conservation assessments for this near-threatened species.
